name: Bookkeeping business
blurb: Keep the books for small businesses, usually remotely and on a monthly retainer
title: How to Start a Bookkeeping Business for Small Businesses
description: How a bookkeeping business makes money, the skills and software needed, where bookkeeping ends and regulated tax work begins, the risks and how to test it.
h1: How to start a bookkeeping business
answer: A bookkeeping business records and reconciles transactions, manages invoices and bills, and prepares reports for small businesses, usually on a monthly fee. It can be run from home with accounting software and a laptop. The catches are that mistakes have real consequences for clients, and in many countries tax filing, audits or calling yourself an accountant are regulated, so you need to know where your service stops.

sections.h: How a bookkeeping business makes money
body: Most bookkeepers charge a monthly retainer based on how many transactions and accounts a client has, or an hourly rate for catch-up work on messy books. Extras can include payroll, invoicing, expense management and month-end reports.

Margin goes to software subscriptions, professional insurance, membership or supervision fees where required, and the time it takes to chase clients for receipts. Fixed monthly fees work only if you scope the work clearly.

ul: Bookkeeping knowledge: double-entry, reconciliations and the accounting software your target clients use. A recognised bookkeeping course or certificate helps win trust.
A computer, secure file storage and good password and data-protection habits; you will hold sensitive financial data.
Professional indemnity insurance in case an error costs a client money.

Knowledge of the rules where you work. In the UK, for example, accountancy service providers must be supervised for anti-money laundering, either by HMRC or a professional body. In the US, anyone paid to prepare federal tax returns needs a PTIN, and only enrolled agents, CPAs and attorneys have unlimited rights to represent clients before the IRS.
Engagement letters that state what you do and do not do, especially around tax returns.

sections.h: Who it suits (and who it doesn't)

head: Suits
Not for
rows: Detail-minded people who like numbers and routine
Anyone who finds repetitive data work draining
People with accounting or admin experience
People hoping to give tax advice without credentials
Someone who wants remote, flexible work
Anyone uncomfortable chasing clients for paperwork

ul: Scope creep: clients will ask for tax advice or filings you may not be qualified or licensed to provide. Know the line and refer out.
Errors: a wrong reconciliation can lead to penalties or bad decisions for the client; insurance and review routines matter.
Late and missing paperwork from clients makes deadlines tight.
Software changes and automation reduce demand for pure data entry; advisory and clean-up work hold value better.
Client concentration: a few large clients can be most of your income.

sections.h: How to test it cheaply first

ol: Check what rules, registration or supervision apply to bookkeepers where you live.
Offer to tidy one month of books for a friend's small business at a real price.
Ask three local business owners what frustrates them about their books today.
Compare the services and pricing structures of bookkeepers in your area.
Pick a niche, such as tradespeople, online sellers or restaurants, and see whether you can reach ten of them.
Register the business, get professional indemnity insurance and any required supervision.
Get certified in one or two widely used accounting software packages.
Write an engagement letter and a fixed-fee menu by transaction volume.
Set up secure document collection and a monthly close checklist.
Build referral links with accountants who need bookkeeping help and can take tax work you cannot.

faq.q: Do I need to be an accountant to start a bookkeeping business?
faq.a: In many places bookkeeping itself is not restricted, but titles like chartered or certified accountant, auditing and some tax services are. Rules differ by country, so check what applies before you advertise.

faq.q: Can bookkeeping be done fully online?
faq.a: Yes. Most bookkeeping now runs on cloud accounting software and shared document folders, so you can serve clients outside your town.
Common models are a monthly fixed fee based on transaction volume, or an hourly rate for catch-up and clean-up work. Fixed fees are easier for clients but need a clear scope.
